question: A certain force acting on a 20 { kg} mass changes its velocity from 5 { m/s} to 2 { m/s} . Calculate the work done by this force.
solution:
The correct answer is __**-210 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Work-Energy Theorem** states that the net **work done** by the forces acting on a body is equal to the change in its **kinetic energy**.
 
• In this problem, the given values are: Mass of the object (**m**) = **20 kg**, Initial velocity (**u**) = **5 m/s**, and Final velocity (**v**) = **2 m/s**.
 
• The **Initial Kinetic Energy** (Ki) is calculated using the formula 1/2 * m * u². Substituting the values: 1/2 * 20 * (5 * 5) = 10 * 25 = **250 Joules**.
 
• The **Final Kinetic Energy** (Kf) is calculated using the formula 1/2 * m * v². Substituting the values: 1/2 * 20 * (2 * 2) = 10 * 4 = **40 Joules**.
